solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food, when chopped, put into portions

indicators.note: put into says the following pieces are placed inside the word for portions

parts.note: cuts are portions, as of meat
as can mean when (as I left = when I left)
hewn means chopped, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: chop the food and divide it into portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'chopped' look like recipe language, but each is a synonym; 'put into' sets both inside the word for portions.
explanation.definitionFit: These kidney-shaped kernels are an example of food, eaten as a snack or in cooking.

clue.text: Bashful bears initially paired for reproduction

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the shy word holds a letter within

parts.note: coy means bashful or shy

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of paired

explanation.surface: Shy bears pair up to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' is a verb, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a reproduction or duplicate of an original.

clue.text: Ingredient of explosive soldier favoured in revolutionary times

indicators.note: in places the soldier and favoured pieces inside the reversed times
revolutionary means the word for times is turned round

parts.note: eras are times or ages
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer
pet means favourite or favoured

explanation.surface: A soldier is in favour in revolutionary times, handling explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: ERAS reversed gives SARE, holding LT and PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, the oxidiser in gunpowder, is a component of an explosive.

clue.text: Flaw reflected in mirror, regretfully

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A defect is regrettably reflected in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters within 'mirror, regretfully'; 'reflected' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or flaw.

clue.text: Case from Nice, second-class with tatty wrapping recently delivered

indicators.note: case from means the outer letters, the casing of Nice
wrapping means the shabby word goes round the class letter

parts.note: worn means shabby or tatty
B is the grade for second-class

explanation.surface: A tatty, second-rate suitcase arrives from Nice in its wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case from' looks like luggage but asks for the casing of Nice, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby has only just been born, delivered recently.

clue.text: Part of plant having cotton on, albeit missing in odd places

parts.note: to twig is to cotton on, to understand

indicators.note: missing in odd places means the first, third and fifth letters go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A plant part has cotton growing on it, though bare in odd spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cotton on' is British slang for understand, which is twig; the even letters of albeit give LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small twig, a slender shoot, is a part of a plant.

clue.text: Path that's used by aircraft on trip

indicators.note: on a trip one falls headlong, so the aircraft word loses its head letter

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: A flight path followed by planes during a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on trip' tells you the aircraft word trips over and loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow way or track, a synonym for a path.

clue.text: A sport in which ball is snatched away and put down

indicators.note: is snatched away means the ball word is taken out of the sport

parts.note: baseball is a sport
taken as written

explanation.surface: In some ball game the ball gets grabbed and placed on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: BASEBALL loses BALL to leave BASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to humiliate or demean them, to put them down.

clue.text: Relation's conclusion — don't argue

definitions.meaning: a relation is a narrative or account, so this is the finish of a tale
an idiom meaning that is final, no more discussion

explanation.surface: A relative's final word: don't argue with me.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the matter is closed, and literally it is the finish of a tale or relation.

clue.text: Hotel this freezing might make Hartlepool questionable

indicators.note: questionable says the letters of the town name are of doubtful order and get rearranged

parts.note: the clue word is used as letters, joined with the answer to make up the town

explanation.surface: A hotel being so cold might give the town of Hartlepool a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus HOTEL rearranges to HARTLEPOOL, a port town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar means extremely cold, like the regions around the poles.

clue.text: Dress to some extent rubbish? Not permitted to say

indicators.note: to say means the words are spoken, so a phrase that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: rubbish is waste and not permitted is banned, giving waste banned

explanation.surface: Someone eyes part of a dress and wonders whether calling it rubbish is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: WASTE BANNED is said aloud and sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The band round the middle of a dress or skirt is a part of the garment, so it is the dress to some extent.

clue.text: Drunk upended for all to see, stuck in another ditch

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the drunk word is turned upside down

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

indicators.note: stuck in places the film rating letter inside the second drunk

parts.note: another drunk, so another sot
U is the universal film classification, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A drunk turned upside down in a ditch, with another stuck there in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means a second drunk, using the same synonym again; U is the British film rating for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss out is to throw away or discard, a synonym for ditch.

clue.text: Cook's wild boar in sauce sent back

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
sent back says the word for sauce is turned round

parts.note: lip is cheek or impudence, which is also sauce

indicators.note: wild means the letters of boar run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook makes a sauce from wild boar and has it returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' means cheek or impudence here, not a condiment; 'sent back' turns that word round and the wild boar goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To parboil is to part-cook food by boiling briefly, so it is a way to cook.

clue.text: Bundle of papers getting left for a bank

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another, here left taking the place of a

parts.note: a sheaf is a bundle of papers

explanation.surface: Someone collects a bundle of papers left for a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link: SHEAF gets L for its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a ledge or sandbank under water, so it can mean a bank.

clue.text: Hour immersed in Art Deco complex regarding geometric form

indicators.note: immersed in places the time letter inside the shuffled style
complex means the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: An hour spent absorbed in an Art Deco building with a geometric design.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ART DECO is OCTAEDR, with H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-faced solid figure is a geometric form.

clue.text: Presumably he's no fan of United financier?

definitions.text: Presumably he's no fan of United
definitions.meaning: a supporter of Manchester City, the rival of Manchester United, would be no fan of United
someone who works in the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A sports fan is presumed to dislike United, and he happens to be a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester City and Manchester United are rival football clubs; the City is also London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A man working in the City of London's financial district is a financier or banker.

clue.text: Director of pit lifted tons in gold layer

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the whole is read upwards
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a seam is a layer of coal or ore

explanation.surface: A mine manager hoists tons out of a gold seam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the tons letter between gold and layer; the pit is the orchestra pit, not a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a conductor, who directs the orchestra in the pit below the stage.

clue.text: Judged for all that time

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless or for all that

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that they were judged for all that time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for all that time' reads as a phrase, but 'for all that' and 'time' split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought can mean considered or reckoned, as in 'I thought it fair', so it means judged.

clue.text: Most of the pay merrily taken from Daily Telegraph wasted, as mine is

indicators.note: merrily means these letters are jumbled up too
wasted means the newspaper's name is wrecked and rearranged
most of means the last letter of the is dropped

explanation.surface: Most of someone's pay goes on the Daily Telegraph, wasted, as theirs is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' says TH and PAY come out of DAILY TELEGRAPH, whose remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine has underground passages called galleries, so it is galleried.

clue.text: How is man to manage never growing up?

parts.note: the reading applied to the word manage leaves man, which is how the clue asks man relates to manage

explanation.surface: A question about how a man is to cope with never growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, AGE LESS: that is how MANAGE becomes MAN, by losing the letters A, G, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never seems to grow older or mature is timeless, never growing up.

clue.text: Withdrawn second edition with plot lacking in book

indicators.note: lacking in means the book letter is missing

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A second edition was withdrawn because the book lacked a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a garden bed, not a storyline; without B it is ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Seceded means formally withdrew from a union or alliance.

clue.text: Fighter's first to lunge in assault

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: to batter is to assault

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of lunge is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer is the first to lunge in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A battler is someone who fights on doggedly, a fighter.

clue.text: Drive a vehicle to the north island for a drink

indicators.note: to the north in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Drive north to an island for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DR + A + CAB reversed is BACARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of rum, so an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Vote on second of referendums, ruling is spot on

indicators.note: on places the voting mark after the letter before it
second of means take the second letter of referendums

parts.note: X is the cross made on a ballot paper
an act is a law or ruling

explanation.surface: A vote after a second referendum delivers a ruling that is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts X after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely accurate, which is what spot on means.

clue.text: Apply after seeing that property

indicators.note: after places the apply word behind the seeing that word

parts.note: as means because or seeing that
to set can mean to apply, as setting one's mind to a task

explanation.surface: Apply after having seen the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing that' is a phrase for AS, not a view of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something owned, a piece of property.

clue.text: Drug money to acquire something like Ecstasy

indicators.note: to acquire means the money word takes in another piece

parts.note: coin is money
ca, circa, means about or something like
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer uses money to buy a drug like ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something like' is circa, about, abbreviated; it is not part of the definition of the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocaine is an example of a drug, a stimulant made from coca leaves.

clue.text: Heard pub became bar

indicators.note: heard means the pub word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an inn is a pub
got can mean became, as in got angry

explanation.surface: Someone heard that the pub turned into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a block of metal, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: Refuse from home over yard

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the home word above the yard letter

parts.note: a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Rubbish comes from the house onto the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the verb, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny is to refuse or turn down a request.

clue.text: Person playing Becker's the one making comeback

indicators.note: playing means the letters of person are shuffled about

parts.note: Boris Becker is German, and der is German for the

explanation.surface: Whoever is playing tennis star Boris Becker is the one staging a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like tennis but it is the anagram signal on PERSON, giving RESPON.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is one who replies, and a comeback is a reply or retort.

clue.text: Good mature beef

parts.note: ripe means mature

explanation.surface: A description of good, well-aged beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is not meat here but a slang complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a complaint or grievance.

clue.text: One's scratching head due to these, perhaps

definitions.text: One's scratching head due to these, perhaps

indicators.note: scratching head means the first letter is scratched out

parts.note: one is a unit, and with 's added gives units

explanation.surface: Someone scratching their head might be doing so because of lice eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: UNITS loses its first letter; the whole clue also describes why someone scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice eggs in the hair make the scalp itch, so they are why one might scratch one's head.

clue.text: Drunk mate? Tiddly, certainly

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Is my friend drunk? A bit tipsy, certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiddly' is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittedly concedes a point, much as certainly does in 'certainly, it was late'.
